title: Lessons from building an agency after freelancing since 2020
primaryKeyword: choosing a branding and marketing agency
metaDescription: Lessons from building an agency after freelancing since 2020 — Altmash's practical guide with steps, mistakes to avoid, key metrics and a 30-day plan.
keywords: choosing a branding and marketing agency
intro: Most advice about choosing a branding and marketing agency is either too generic or written by people who have never had to hit a monthly target with it. I am Altmash, and everything in this guide comes from running live brands across fashion, ethnic wear, footwear, perfume and community platforms.
You will find the framework I use with clients, real examples from brands I have worked on, the numbers worth tracking and a plan to put it into action without a big team.
takeaways: Keep every account and file in your own name.
Hire on live proof, not decks.
One owner across brand, site and ads beats three vendors.

sections.heading: Why choosing a branding and marketing agency matters more than most founders think
paragraphs: The right agency gives you strategy and execution under one owner, so your website, creatives and ad spend push in the same direction. The wrong one gives you polished decks and a monthly invoice with nothing that moves revenue.
Because an agency sits close to your money, the relationship needs structure: a clear scope, a weekly scoreboard and one person accountable for outcomes, not just deliverables.

The good news is that none of this needs a big team. It needs clear decisions, a weekly rhythm and someone who owns the result after launch — which is exactly how I run agency for the brands I manage.

sections.heading: How to approach agency, step by step
paragraphs: Here is the process I follow. The order matters: each step removes a reason for the next one to fail.
Do not skip the early steps to get to the exciting part. In my experience, most agency problems that look like execution issues are really decisions that were never made at the start.
bullets: Write the brief: goal, budget, current numbers, what has been tried and what success looks like in 90 days.
Shortlist by proof: ask for live brands they still manage, not just portfolio screenshots.
Run a paid trial: a four to six week sprint on one clear problem tells you more than any pitch.
Agree a scoreboard: three to five metrics reviewed every week in the same document.
Define ownership: ad accounts, domains, pixels and design files stay in your name from day one.
Review at 90 days: keep, expand or exit based on the scoreboard, not on how busy things felt.

sections.heading: Selling to Indian and global buyers
paragraphs: Indian buyers are mobile-first, value-conscious and quick to message a brand on WhatsApp before they buy. Page speed on patchy networks, clear pricing, easy payment options and fast replies are part of agency, not separate from it.
Festive seasons, regional preferences and cash-on-delivery habits also shape results. Plan your calendar around them instead of treating every month the same.

sections.heading: The numbers that actually matter for agency
paragraphs: Pick a small set of numbers and review them every week in the same place. I prefer five metrics the whole team understands over a dashboard nobody opens.
Look at trends over four to eight weeks rather than daily swings, and always tie the numbers back to revenue or qualified leads.
bullets: Revenue or qualified leads from agency-run channels
Time from brief to live campaign
Conversion rate on pages the agency owns

sections.heading: Real examples from the field
paragraphs: One example from my own work: An Android fintech app cut drop-off by rewriting KYC screens in plain language and matching Play Store screenshots to the first session.
For agency, the takeaway is to treat proof and clarity as part of the work, not as decoration on top of it.
Another: An interior studio’s website looked premium but leaked leads — a simpler brief form plus WhatsApp routing doubled qualified conversations.
The details differ by category, but the principle holds: when the brand, the page and the channel tell one story, agency becomes cheaper and more predictable.

sections.heading: How much time and money agency takes
paragraphs: In India, small brands typically spend ₹30,000 to ₹1,50,000 a month on agency retainers depending on scope, with ad spend on top. A four to six week trial on a single problem is the cheapest way to find out whether the fit is real.

These ranges are starting points, not quotes. The right number depends on your category, your margins and how much of the work your team can handle in-house. What matters most is committing to a test long enough to learn from it.

sections.heading: Putting it into action: a 30-day plan
paragraphs: If you want to move quickly, here is how I would sequence the first month.
At the end of the month you will have real data instead of opinions — and a clear picture of where to invest next.
bullets: Week 1: Write the brief and shortlist by proof.
Week 3: Agree a scoreboard and define ownership.
Week 4: Review at 90 days, then review your metrics and decide what to keep.

conclusion: If you take one thing from this guide, let it be this: agency compounds when it is treated as a system. Fix the inputs, keep a simple scoreboard and give each change enough time to show results.
If you want help applying this to your brand, message me on WhatsApp. I am Altmash, and I build and run brands end to end — website, identity, ads and the systems that keep them growing.

faq.q: Is an agency better than a freelancer?
faq.a: A freelancer is great for a single skill like design or ads. An agency makes sense when you need strategy, creative, website and paid media working together with one accountable owner.

faq.q: What should an agency retainer include?
faq.a: A clear scope of deliverables, a weekly or fortnightly performance review, named people on your account and a notice period. Ad spend should be billed separately and paid directly from your own account.

faq.q: How do I know if my agency is working?
faq.a: Look at the scoreboard you agreed at the start. If qualified leads, revenue or acquisition cost are not improving after 90 days of consistent work, the plan or the partner needs to change.

faq.q: Can I handle agency myself or should I hire help?
faq.a: You can start yourself if you follow a clear process and review the numbers every week. Bring in help when the work starts eating time you should spend on product and sales, or when results plateau and you cannot see why.

faq.q: Does Altmash work with brands outside India?
faq.a: Yes. Altmash works with Indian and international brands on branding, websites, Shopify, ads and full brand management, usually coordinated over WhatsApp and video calls.
